title: Hello and goodbye (Begrüßen und verabschieden)
summary: Greet people at the right time of day, formally and informally, the Munich way included.
goals: Greet people and say goodbye, formally and informally
Ask how someone is and answer

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1: Welcome to A1 (Hallo! and Tschüss!)

sections.title: Greetings through the day
sections.text:
- [[Guten Morgen!]] in the morning, until about 11
- [[Guten Tag!]] during the day, polite
- [[Guten Abend!]] from about 6 pm
- [[Gute Nacht!]] only when someone goes to bed
- [[Hallo!]] any time, informal, and very common at work too

To say goodbye: [[Tschüss!]] (informal) or [[Auf Wiedersehen!]] (polite).

sections.title: In Munich
sections.text: In Bavaria you will hear [[Grüß Gott!]] (a polite hello in shops and offices) and [[Servus!]] (informal; it means both hi and bye). You don't have to use them, but now you will recognise them.

sections.title: du or Sie?
sections.text:
German has two words for 'you':

- [[du]] for friends, family, children, and many younger colleagues
- [[Sie]] (always with a capital S) for strangers, officials, older people, and at work until someone offers [[du]]

When in doubt, start with [[Sie]]. Many startups and tech teams use [[du]] from the first day.
The same system as Russian ты / Вы and Armenian դու / Դուք. The polite [[Sie]] is always written with a capital letter, a bit like the polite Вы in a letter.
Answer in the same form you were asked: [[du]] with [[Und dir?]], [[Sie]] with [[Und Ihnen?]]. Mixing them sounds odd.

items.question: 9 am, you walk into a bakery. What do you say?
items.explanation: Guten Morgen until about 11. Gute Nacht is only for bedtime.

items.question: Your friend is going to bed. What do you say?
items.explanation: Gute Nacht when someone goes to bed; Guten Abend to greet someone in the evening.

items.question: You meet your manager's manager for the first time. How do you ask how they are?
items.explanation: A first meeting with a senior person: use Sie. Wie geht es Ihnen? is the polite form.
Wie geht es Ihnen? Ihnen is the polite 'you' here, always with a capital I.

items.text: Hallo, wie geht's? - Gut, danke. Und ___?
items.explanation: Wie geht's? is informal, so answer informally: Und dir? (polite: Und Ihnen?)
